title: Introduction to Human-Robot Systems
term: Winter 2022 (first offered Fall 2022 per repo; robotics.umich.edu lists Winter 2022)
weeklyTopics: Week 1: Course intro; Lab 1 - user interface control input design
Week 2: Perception and user interfaces, scholarly articles/presentations; Lab 2 - UI
Week 3: Communication (verbal/non-verbal); Lab 3 - non-verbal posture-based robot control
Week 4: Communication - levels of control, teleoperation; Lab 4 - non-verbal
Week 5: Communication - haptics, memos; Lab 5 - human mental models (Amazon Astro)
Week 6: Mental models, decision making, situation awareness, automation, trust; Lab 6 - Astro
Week 7: Situation awareness, automation, trust; library research and source use; Lab 7 - stakeholder interviews
Week 8: Project management; Exam 1; Lab 8 - stakeholder interviews
Week 9: Socially engaged design, problem statements & requirements; Lab 9
Week 10: Robot embodiments and design ideation, usefulness and usability; Lab 10 - design ideation
Week 11: Usefulness and usability, user interface design; Lab 11 - usability study
Week 12: Team meetings, ethics; Lab 12 - usability study
Week 13: Risk assessment, hot topics in HRI; Lab 13 - final project work
Week 14: Final project memo/presentation workshops; Lab 14 - final project work
Week 15: Exam 2, course reflection and evaluations
workloadNotes: Combines lectures, hands-on hardware labs (custom Arduino UI controllers, Raspberry Pi non-verbal communication robot, Amazon Astro), and a multi-week socially-engaged design final project involving real stakeholder interviews and a usability study. Two exams (Week 8 and Week 15).
prerequisitesText: Introductory course for robotics majors, no other prerequisites stated.
